rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13 (body region, above the maintainer fence): 'M2 used this without naming it: **find is easier than judge**.' A literal M[0-9] module-numbering reference in body prose -- the exact shape the rule's stated mechanical grep targets ('Pre-ship grep on body above the maintainer fence: M[0-9] + module-name refs -> each hit moves to the module file or dies'). Neither named carve-out fits: this isn't an arc lecture whose SUBJECT is the arc, and 'M2' isn't a map-position phrase. The maintainer block (line 25) argues an exemption ('supplementary surface, not a lecture body, so check_lectures §3 sequencing ban doesn't bind... backward-naming of a lived moment, not sequencing') and the exemption has real substance -- the rule's three banned examples ('M3 reads this file', 'gets its full name at M5', 'M3 starts with a feature you're shipping') are all FORWARD bridges that pre-empt a downstream teaching moment; this is a BACKWARD retroactive-naming of an already-lived exercise, structurally the opposite hazard. But the exemption is self-declared in the maintainer's own prose, not compendium-confirmed, and a blind pre-ship grep (the rule's own stated enforcement mechanism) would still flag it regardless of direction. Judgment call, not a clean pass.
